# Traceability

<!-- Generated by tools/common/check/check-traceability.py from docs/sysml/, the
     `/// Verifies:` tags on the checks and docs/certification/coverage-*.json.
     Do not edit: run the script, which `cargo xtask check` runs with --check. -->

The certified item's requirements in three levels, each naming its parent, and the checks that name each one. The system level is the Security Target's objectives (SECURITY-TARGET.md §4.1), the safety manual's assumed safety requirements (SAFETY-MANUAL.md §2) and the goal (`docs/sysml/01-requirements.sysml`). The high level (`H.*`) is what a subsystem of the item promises at its interface (`docs/sysml/13-item-requirements.sysml`); the low level (`L.*`) is what one unit of code does. IMPLEMENTATION.md W-8 is the design.

A requirement is verified on an architecture when a check names it (`/// Verifies:` on the check's function) and that check's statements were executed in the architecture's coverage run. The columns per architecture say: *reached*, *not reached*, *not built* (the check is another architecture's), *not measured* (the coverage evidence was written before it recorded the checks' own statements), or that the verifier is a host test or an xtask gate rather than a boot. The boot's `FERRIX-BOOT-OK`, the third link, is what `cargo xtask test-boot` gates on each architecture.

Coverage evidence recording the checks: x86-64, AArch64, ARMv7-A.

## Summary

| Level | Written | Named by a check | Unverified, in the baseline |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| High (`H.*`) | 123 | 72 | 51 |
| Low (`L.*`) | 804 | 533 | 271 |

1645 functions of the item are named as a low-level requirement's unit. Of the item's product functions, the gate counts those a requirement names, the *accessors* -- one statement or one expression, no branch point and no `unsafe`, whose behaviour is the requirement of the function they serve -- the check code that still lives in product files (listed below), and the rest, which no requirement names. That last list changes with every function written, so it is printed by `--report`, not kept here; in a subsystem whose low-level requirements are complete it must be empty, and the gate fails otherwise.

| Product functions | Count |
|---|---:|
| Named by a low-level requirement | 1647 |
| Accessors, covered by the requirement they serve | 856 |
| Check code in a product file | 65 |
| Named by none | 883 |

Subsystems whose low-level requirements are complete: `arch::aarch64`, `arch::x86_64`, `claim`, `console`, `device`, `early`, `iommu`, `mm`, `object`, `smp`, `trap`, `user`, `vmap`.

### Check code in product files

Functions that are checks, or serve only checks, and live in a product file, so that no `Verifies:` tag may go on them and the item's size counts them. Each is to move into a check file; until it does it is listed here, in `tools/common/data/traceability-units.json`, and not reported as a function no requirement names.

| Function | Why it is check code |
|---|---|
| `arch::aarch64::check_distributor` | The architecture's entry to the GICv2 distributor check (arch/arm_common/gicv2/check.rs, F-50), which main.rs calls through the arch interface every architecture provides; it runs the check on a GICv2 and says it did not run on a GICv3. |
| `arch::aarch64::check_exception_entry` | The architecture's answer to the generic boot's exception-entry check: nothing to check here, since no exception finds the kernel on a program's stack. Part of the arch interface every architecture provides. |
| `arch::aarch64::check_machine` | The architecture's entry to its machine check (arch/aarch64/check.rs), which main.rs calls through the arch interface every architecture provides; it runs the check and nothing else. |
| `arch::aarch64::gic::enabled_for_check` | Reads a line's enable back from whichever GIC driver the boot chose, for the machine check's masking case; it needs the driver choice private to gic.rs. |
| `arch::aarch64::gic::gicv3::enabled_for_check` | Reads a GICv3 line's enable bit back for the machine check; it needs the register windows private to gicv3.rs. |
| `arch::aarch64::gic::gicv3::idle_line_for_check` | Finds a GICv3 line nothing has enabled for the machine check; it needs the register windows private to gicv3.rs. |
| `arch::aarch64::gic::idle_line_for_check` | Finds a line nothing has enabled, for the machine check's masking case; it needs the driver choice private to gic.rs. |
| `arch::x86_64::check_exception_entry` | It only runs the paranoid, syscall, gdt and trap checks' run functions, for main.rs's stage 3; it can move into a check file under arch::x86_64. |
| `arch::x86_64::console::loop_back` | Serves only interrupt remapping's checks R5 and G3's service once (iommu/check.rs): it loops one byte back through the port to its own receiver. It needs the port's registers, private to arch/x86_64/console.rs, so it stays beside them. |
| `arch::x86_64::cpu::forbid_user_access` | Closes SMAP's window through arch::forbid_user_access, whose only callers are user/check.rs's checks. |
| `arch::x86_64::cpu::permit_user_access` | Opens SMAP's window through arch::permit_user_access, whose only callers are user/check.rs's checks of the window; the kernel's own user copies do not use it. |
| `arch::x86_64::cpu::write_breakpoint_address` | Arms a debug register; called only from arch/x86_64/paranoid/check.rs, whose breakpoint checks are its reason to exist. |
| `arch::x86_64::cpu::write_dr7` | Enables or clears the debug registers' slots; called only from arch/x86_64/paranoid/check.rs. |
| `arch::x86_64::identity_map_live` | Its only caller is main.rs's stage 2 check, which runs only when the boot checks. |
| `arch::x86_64::loop_back_console` | The x86-64 hook iommu::remapping::LiveLine::loop_back names for checks R5 and G3 (iommu/check.rs): it runs console::loop_back with the port quiet. Registered from console_receive_irq with the line's other hooks, so it stays beside them. |
| `arch::x86_64::paranoid::debug_hook` | Only a breakpoint target and counter for paranoid/check.rs's check_breakpoints_do_not_nest; every kernel #DB calls it so the check can arm a breakpoint on the handler's own path. |
| `arch::x86_64::speculation::check` | The x86-64 half of arch::speculation_check::check (machine::check), with no product caller: it runs VERW once to show the exit paths' operand is accepted. It reaches speculation.rs's private plan. |
| `arch::x86_64::speculation::clear_cpu_buffers` | Called only by speculation::check, to run VERW once for the boot check. |
| `arch::x86_64::trap::breakpoint` | Its only callers are main.rs's check_breakpoint, which raises int3 twice for stage 3's check. |
| `console::input::check` | The receive ring's check (FX-0305, the `input` line), run from main.rs before the port's interrupt is installed. It fills and empties RING and reads HELD and OVERRUNS, private to input.rs; as a child module, console/input/check.rs, it could read them and verify L.console.20. |
| `console::input::take_check_byte` | Serves only checks R5 and G3 (iommu/check.rs): it takes the check's looped-back byte off the front of the receive ring, so it never reaches a reader. It needs the ring, private to console/input.rs. |
| `console::output::check` | The transmit check (FX-0504, the `output` line), run from main.rs once tasks can wait. It reads BY_INTERRUPT, BY_WRITER, HELD and waits on WRITERS, private to output.rs; as a child module, console/output/check.rs, it could read them and verify L.console.9 and L.console.10. |
| `console::output::with_port_quiet` | Serves only checks R5 and G3 (iommu/check.rs): it holds the port's transmit side quiet, under the port's lock, while one byte is looped back. It needs the port lock and its ring, private to console/output.rs. |
| `early::EarlyMemory::read_physical_byte` | Stage 1's check_direct_map, in stages_check.rs, reads the image's first bytes through it; nothing else calls it. It can move into a check file of early's. |
| `early::EarlyMemory::translate` | Called only by stage 1's checks in main.rs (check_early_mapper, check_no_early_window_wraps); it reads EarlyMemory's private walk state. |
| `iommu::Domain::provoke_interrupt` | Serves only checks R1 to R3 (device/check.rs): it clears the unit's faults and registers the interrupt fault the check is about to provoke. It needs the domain's private fault-clearing loop, as Domain::provoke does for DMA. |
| `iommu::record_provoked_interrupt` | Serves only checks R1 to R3, through Domain::provoke_interrupt: it records the stream and reason a check provokes and says so. It needs PROVOKED_INTERRUPTS, private to iommu.rs, which provoked() reads. |
| `iommu::remapping::close_check_window` | Serves only checks R1 and R2: it closes open_check_window's window. Beside it for the same reason. |
| `iommu::remapping::open_check_window` | Serves only checks R1 and R2 (device/check.rs): it opens the window inside which a delivery of the check vector 0xFC is the check's, not stray. It needs the window's statics, private to iommu/remapping.rs, which the vector's handler reads. |
| `iommu::vtd::check_planted_completion_error` | Serves only the stage 10 check of a completion error (iommu/check.rs check_completion_errors, L.iommu.48): it plants ICE in the unit's software mirror of FSTS and drives two invalidations through it. It needs the unit's mirror and counters, private to vtd.rs, so it stays beside them. |
| `iommu::vtd::leave_queue_on_and_stop` | Serves only the stage 10 check of a queue firmware left on (iommu/check.rs check_firmware_left_on, L.iommu.51): it puts a unit's queue in the state such firmware leaves it in, then calls the product path stop_firmware. It needs the unit's registers and frames, private to vtd.rs, so it stays beside them. |
| `mm::FrameWindow::kept` | A check's frame window: frames kept since it opened. Every caller is a check file; it reads Held, which reads the heap and route counters private to mm.rs. |
| `mm::FrameWindow::report_at` | Prints a window's heap and per-route movement for a failing check, through FrameWindow::report; check files only. |
| `mm::Held::now` | The frame window's settled read of free frames, slab pages and route counters, for FrameWindow and held_frames, whose callers are all check files. It reads HEAP and ROUTE_COUNTS, private to mm.rs. |
| `mm::claim_frame` | Takes back a frame a check has just given up (smp/check.rs, user/rmap_check.rs), to prove it was free; no product caller. |
| `mm::count` | Counts frames per allocation route into ROUTE_COUNTS. Called on the product allocation paths, so it cannot move, but only checks read what it writes (Held::now, and user_tables_given_back for smp/check.rs's table check). |
| `mm::frame_state` | What the frame allocator records for a frame, for mm/check.rs's frame-0 check and user/edge_check.rs; no product caller. |
| `mm::print_frame_delta` | Prints which way a check's frame count missed, for a check about to fail; called only from check files. Nothing private keeps it in mm.rs; it can move to mm/check.rs with FrameWindow. |
| `mm::unlinked::UnlinkedTables::frames` | The frames a list holds, for smp/check.rs's check that an unmap's tables are still held; it reads the list's private links. |
| `object::as_if_draining_elsewhere` | Runs a check's closure as though another context were draining disposed objects (object/check.rs, block_ring/check.rs). It sets the DISPOSING flag dispose reads, which is private to object/mod.rs. |
| `object::process::Exit::for_check` | An end no process has, for object/pin/check.rs's budget checks; it needs Exit's private constructor. |
| `sched::trip::answered` | A stamp point of the seam's depth-1 trace (block_ring/trip_check.rs). Unarmed it loads TRACING and returns; only hop_check arms it. It sits in block_ring's complete() under the disk's state lock, which is what keeps it in product code. |
| `sched::trip::arm` | Raises the seam's depth-1 trace and zeroes its counts; its only caller is block_ring/hop_check.rs. |
| `sched::trip::bell` | A stamp point of the seam's depth-1 trace, on the ring task's bell to the driver. Unarmed it loads TRACING and returns; only hop_check arms it. |
| `sched::trip::count` | Counts switches, root writes, IPIs and device interrupts for the seam's trace, called on those product paths. Unarmed it loads TRACING and returns; only hop_check arms it, and only trip_check reads the counts. |
| `sched::trip::counted` | Reads the trace's counts for block_ring/trip_check.rs, its only caller. |
| `sched::trip::disarm` | Lowers the seam's depth-1 trace; its only caller is block_ring/hop_check.rs. |
| `sched::trip::done` | Ends a traced trip and hands its stamps to block_ring/trip_check.rs, its only caller through hop_check. |
| `sched::trip::interrupt_queued` | A stamp point of the seam's depth-1 trace, in Line::fire before the packet is queued. Unarmed it loads TRACING and returns; only hop_check arms it. |
| `sched::trip::issued` | A stamp point of the seam's depth-1 trace: the check calls a read. Its only caller is block_ring/hop_check.rs. |
| `sched::trip::name` | Records which wait queue a traced trip uses; reached only from stamp points while the trace is armed. |
| `sched::trip::now_here` | Reads the counter and the processor for a stamp; reached only from stamp points while the trace is armed. |
| `sched::trip::on_ring` | A stamp point of the seam's depth-1 trace, as the ring task puts a request on the ring. Unarmed it loads TRACING and returns; only hop_check arms it. |
| `sched::trip::port_rung` | A stamp point of the seam's depth-1 trace, in port_queue on the ring's kernel port. Unarmed it loads TRACING and returns; only hop_check arms it. |
| `sched::trip::port_taken` | A stamp point of the seam's depth-1 trace, in port_wait on the driver's port. Unarmed it loads TRACING and returns; only hop_check arms it. |
| `sched::trip::queued` | A stamp point of the seam's depth-1 trace, as a read is queued. Unarmed it loads TRACING and returns; only hop_check arms it. |
| `sched::trip::reader_running` | A stamp point of the seam's depth-1 trace, as the reader runs again. Unarmed it loads TRACING and returns; only hop_check arms it. |
| `sched::trip::ring_running` | A stamp point of the seam's depth-1 trace, as the ring task runs. Unarmed it loads TRACING and returns; only hop_check arms it. |
| `sched::trip::slept` | Counts sleeps on the traced queues ended by a wake or by the recheck, called from WaitQueue::wait_until_deadline. Unarmed it loads TRACING and returns; only hop_check arms it, and only trip_check reads the counts. |
| `sched::trip::stamp` | Stores one stamp if the traced trip has reached it; reached only from stamp points while the trace is armed. |
| `sched::trip::store` | Writes a stamp slot; reached only from stamp points while the trace is armed. |
| `smp::next_job` | The work run_everywhere handed out that a secondary has not done yet. Only stage 4's checks hand work out (smp/check.rs); secondary_main, product code, calls this in its wait loop until the scheduler takes the processor over, so it stays beside that loop and the JOB state both read. |
| `smp::run_everywhere` | Runs a function on every online processor at once and waits for each: how stage 4's checks run on every processor, and nothing else calls it. It writes the JOB state secondary_main's product loop reads through next_job, so moving it into smp/check.rs would leave the product loop reading a check file's state. |
| `vmap::check_failed_device_map` | A check, called from mm/check.rs's check_vmap, that a device mapping failing part way leaves nothing mapped. It uses vmap.rs's private reserve, release and map_reserved; moved into a check file it verifies L.mm.52. |
| `vmap::check_invariants` | The arena's consistency check, called from mm/check.rs's check_vmap; it reads the private ARENA. Moved into a check file it verifies L.mm.53. |

## High-level requirements

### Memory (`H.MEM`)

| Id | Statement | Criterion | Parent | Verified by | x86-64 | AArch64 | ARMv7-A |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `H.MEM.1` | A user address space shall translate a user virtual address only to a frame its own mappings name, so that one address in two address spaces reaches two frames unless a VMO both map shares one. | Of N reads of one user address, made alternately in two address spaces that each wrote a different value there, all N return the reading space's own value and none the other's (the boot's `spaces` line, N = 128). | O.ISOLATE, ASR-1 | `src/kernel/src/user/check.rs::check_two_tasks_keep_their_own_address_spaces` | reached | reached | reached |
| `H.MEM.2` | No mapping of kernel memory shall be accessible from user mode: a user-mode read, write or instruction fetch at a kernel address shall end in a fault delivered to the thread, never in the access. | A program that reads, writes and jumps to a kernel-half address is ended with SIGSEGV each time, 3 of 3, on every architecture, and the kernel's memory at that address is unchanged. | O.ISOLATE, ASR-1 | *baselined* | — | — | — |
| `H.MEM.3` | On every processor the kernel shall run with its own access to user pages refused outside the window a user copy opens: SMEP and SMAP on x86-64, PAN on AArch64 where the processor implements it. ARMv7-A has no such control (AoU-6). | The boot reports SMEP on and SMAP on (x86-64), or PAN on where offered (AArch64), for each of the N online processors; a kernel read of a user page outside the window faults. | O.ISOLATE, ASR-1 | *baselined* | — | — | — |
| `H.MEM.4` | Once bring-up has dropped the loader's identity map, no leaf mapping under the kernel's own root table or the identity root shall be both writable and executable. | The boot's sweep of every leaf mapping under the kernel's root and the identity root counts N mappings, E > 0 of them executable, and 0 both writable and executable (the `w^x` line). | O.WXN, ASR-2 | `src/kernel/src/mm/check.rs::sweep_w_xor_x` | reached | reached | reached |
| `H.MEM.5` | No mapping of the frames that hold the kernel's text and read-only data, the direct map's alias of them included, shall be writable. | The boot's sweep of every mapping of those frames finds 0 writable, and finds the direct map aliasing every byte of them (the `sealed` line). | O.WXN, ASR-2 | `src/kernel/src/mm/check.rs::check_sealed_image` | reached | reached | reached |
| `H.MEM.6` | A physical frame shall hold only zeros when it is committed to a VMO, mapped into a user address space for the first time, or made a page table. | A frame written with a pattern, freed and committed again reads 0 non-zero bytes of its 4096 before the new owner's first write, for a VMO page and for a page table alike. | O.SCRUB, ASR-5 | *baselined* | — | — | — |
| `H.MEM.7` | A page-table frame an unmap empties shall not return to the frame allocator until the TLB invalidation that covers the unmap has been made. | A page table an unmap empties is still held, not freed, until the shootdown covering it completes: 0 tables freed before it, and exactly the tables it emptied given back by it. | O.ISOLATE, ASR-1 | `src/kernel/src/smp/check.rs::tables_wait_for_their_shootdown` | reached | reached | reached |
| `H.MEM.8` | After a fork, a write by the parent or the child to a private page shall not be visible to the other. | The `cow` program, in which each side writes a page both shared, exits 61 (neither saw the other's write). | O.ISOLATE, ASR-1 | `src/kernel/src/syscall/check.rs::check_a_copy_on_write_page_is_copied_for_the_side_that_writes` | reached | reached | reached |
| `H.MEM.9` | Every frame an address space, a VMO or a process holds shall return to the frame allocator when the last reference to it goes. | After each memory and program check, the free frame count is what it was before: 0 frames leaked, per check (the `objects`, `uaccess` and `exits` lines). | O.QUOTA | *baselined* | — | — | — |
| `H.MEM.10` | Every interface that maps a physical range a caller names shall refuse a range that touches the kernel image. | Requests naming the image's first page, its last page and a range straddling its end are each refused, 0 accepted, at stages 1, 2 and 6. | O.ISOLATE, O.WXN | *baselined* | — | — | — |

| `L.btrfs.102` | An operation the metadata room cannot hold, with the commit's reserve and the global reserve, shall be refused with NoSpace before its first edit, and an operation that frees space may still use the global reserve. | Creates until the trees are full end in NoSpace with the transaction not aborted, the commit succeeds, 64 unlinks succeed, and a create after their commit succeeds. | H.STORE.6 | `ferrix_btrfs_write::volume::WriteVolume::admit`, `ferrix_btrfs_write::volume::WriteVolume::commit_reserve`, `ferrix_btrfs_write::volume::WriteVolume::guarded_with`, `ferrix_btrfs_write::volume::WriteVolume::operation_with`, `ferrix_btrfs_write::grow::WriteVolume::meta_room`, `ferrix_btrfs_write::grow::WriteVolume::tree_headroom` | `src/lib/fs/btrfs-write/src/tests/full.rs::creates_on_full_trees_are_refused_and_a_deletion_still_makes_room` | host test | host test | host test |
| `L.btrfs.103` | A data write on full trees shall be refused with NoSpace, aborting nothing. | After the trees are filled, 64 KiB writes end in NoSpace with the transaction not aborted, and the commit checks clean. | H.STORE.6 | `ferrix_btrfs_write::volume::WriteVolume::admit`, `ferrix_btrfs_write::volume::WriteVolume::operation_with` | `src/lib/fs/btrfs-write/src/tests/full.rs::a_data_write_on_full_trees_aborts_nothing` | host test | host test | host test |
| `L.btrfs.104` | A data write that needs a new metadata chunk shall succeed or be refused with NoSpace, aborting nothing. | With metadata used until the next edit must make a chunk, a write of the data room succeeds or is NoSpace, the transaction is not aborted, and the commit checks clean. | H.STORE.6 | `ferrix_btrfs_write::volume::WriteVolume::ensure_space`, `ferrix_btrfs_write::volume::WriteVolume::guarded_with`, `ferrix_btrfs_write::volume::WriteVolume::grow` | `src/lib/fs/btrfs-write/src/tests/full.rs::a_metadata_chunk_made_during_a_write_of_the_room_aborts_nothing` | host test | host test | host test |
| `L.btrfs.105` | Through a mount, a write to a full volume shall be refused with ENOSPC at exactly the room statfs offered, keeping what was written. | Through ferrix-btrfs-vfs, writes stop with ENOSPC at the byte statfs offered, the file holds every byte written, and after an unlink a 1 MiB file is written and read back after remounting. | H.STORE.6 | `ferrix_btrfs_write::volume::WriteVolume::admit`, `ferrix_btrfs_write::grow::WriteVolume::data_room` | `src/lib/fs/btrfs-vfs/src/tests/rw.rs::a_full_volume_answers_enospc_and_stays_usable` | host test | host test | host test |

| `L.btrfs.108` | An operation of the write path whose allocation is refused shall answer OutOfMemory, and either leave the transaction as it was or abort it, so that the volume reopens at its last commit. | With each allocation of a script of eleven file operations and a commit on a populated volume failed once in turn, every failing operation answers OutOfMemory; where the transaction was not aborted, the script resumed from that operation ends with the fs tree an undisturbed run makes; where it was, the volume reopens at the commit before the script with its fs tree; every volume checks clean. | H.STORE.7 | `ferrix_btrfs_write::volume::WriteVolume::guarded_with`, `ferrix_btrfs_write::volume::WriteVolume::operation_with`, `ferrix_btrfs_write::volume::WriteVolume::abort_with`, `ferrix_btrfs_write::open::WriteVolume::abort` | `src/lib/fs/btrfs-write/src/tests/oom.rs::a_transaction_out_of_memory_aborts_or_changes_nothing` | host test | host test | host test |
| `L.btrfs.109` | WriteVolume::open shall answer OutOfMemory when an allocation is refused, having written nothing to the device. | With each allocation of opening the blank and the populated volume failed in turn, once and from then on, each open succeeds or answers OutOfMemory, and the device then opens at the same generation with the same fs tree and checks clean. | H.STORE.7 | `ferrix_btrfs_write::open::WriteVolume::open`, `ferrix_btrfs_write::open::WriteVolume::open_committed`, `ferrix_btrfs_write::open::WriteVolume::load_block_groups`, `ferrix_btrfs_write::open::WriteVolume::load_free_space` | `src/lib/fs/btrfs-write/src/tests/oom.rs::opening_out_of_memory_answers_out_of_memory` | host test | host test | host test |
